target_pattern: Use future forms like sera estara llamara and querra to express present speculation uncertainty and rhetorical wondering rather than literal future time.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Treating future tense only as later time and missing speculative meaning in present context.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Spanish future forms can signal uncertainty right now in questions and reactions. This gives a natural might/could/I wonder tone.
target_pattern_formula: action guess: quien llamara or quien estara tocando
interpretation guess: que querra decir con eso
natural_examples: Por que estara tan callada hoy?

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as instructed.
drills: Base: Quien sera? -> change noun idea to a phone call.
Base: Quien llamara? -> change to location question about Juan.
Base: Donde estara Marta? -> change subject to plural ellos.
Base: Que querra decir con eso? -> change pronoun to plural ellos.
Base: Por que estara enojado? -> change adjective to cansado.
Base: Quien estara en la puerta? -> change place to afuera.
Base: Donde estaran mis llaves? -> change object to mis lentes.
Base: Que querran ahora? -> change to singular formal usted.
Base: Por que llamara el jefe? -> change noun to cliente.
Base: Quien escribira a esta hora? -> change verb to trabajar.
Base: Donde estara el documento? -> change noun to plural los documentos.
Base: Que querra decir este mensaje? -> change demonstrative to ese.
Base: Por que estaran preguntando eso? -> change subject to singular el.
Base: Quien estara tocando la puerta? -> change object to el timbre.
Base: Donde habremos dejado el cargador? -> change object to las llaves.

contrastive_discrimination.instructions: Choose the option that matches speculative meaning.
prompts: I wonder who it is. (Quien sera? vs Quien es?)
I wonder where Ana is. (Donde estara Ana? vs Donde esta Ana?)
Who might be calling right now? (Quien llamara ahora? vs Quien llama ahora?)
What might he mean by that? (Que querra decir con eso? vs Que quiere decir con eso?)
Why could they be upset? (Por que estaran molestos? vs Por que estan molestos?)
I wonder who is outside. (Quien estara afuera? vs Quien esta afuera?)
Where could my wallet be? (Donde estara mi cartera? vs Donde esta mi cartera?)
What might they want? (Que querran? vs Que quieren?)
Why might she be so quiet? (Por que estara tan callada? vs Por que esta tan callada?)
Who could be at the office now? (Quien estara en la oficina ahora? vs Quien esta en la oficina ahora?)

common_errors.mistake: Future form interpreted only as literal future time
common_errors.why_it_happens: Learners memorize one default meaning for future tense.
common_errors.correct_spanish: In context sera and estara can express present speculation.

common_errors.mistake: Present indicative used in rhetorical guessing questions
common_errors.correct_spanish: Use speculative future when you are genuinely unsure.

common_errors.mistake: Overusing speculative future in normal factual questions
common_errors.correct_spanish: Reserve this pattern for uncertainty or wondering tone.

common_errors.mistake: Avoiding querra decir because it feels advanced
common_errors.why_it_happens: Preference for literal quiere decir only.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Que querra decir con eso is common and natural.

common_errors.why_it_happens: Low familiarity with forms during fast writing.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Keep forms consistent in your output format for practice.

common_errors.mistake: No distinction between certainty and speculation
common_errors.why_it_happens: English phrasing often hides this contrast.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Future speculation softens certainty and adds doubt.

common_errors.mistake: Trying to force subjunctive for every uncertainty meaning
common_errors.why_it_happens: Uncertainty is linked only to subjunctive in study notes.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Future indicative can also mark uncertainty in these formulas.

common_errors.mistake: Building only statements and avoiding question form
common_errors.why_it_happens: Learners focus on translation not discourse use.
common_errors.correct_spanish: This pattern is especially frequent in questions.

common_errors.mistake: Using speculative future despite confirmed evidence
common_errors.correct_spanish: Use present or past when facts are already known.

common_errors.why_it_happens: Future morphology is auto-interpreted as later time.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Train recognition that many sera/estara lines refer to now.
